hip_flex.source: SetForSet Hanging Leg Raise: "Raise your legs to parallel with the ground" - this means a 90-degree angle between the torso and legs; 0 is the straight hang

knee_flex.source: the exercise is a straight-leg raise by name and by every cited guide's description; no source gives an exact degree, so a small natural give (0 to 10 degrees) is illustrative, inside the AAOS knee row (rig/ranges.ts)

muscles.peakSource: American Sport & Fitness Association, "The Leg Raise: Hip Flexors or Abs?": spinal flexion happens during the leg raise's posterior pelvic tilt, where the abs engage to curl the spine as the legs come up, so ab effort is highest near the top of the lift where that curl happens

mistake.name: Swing and short-change it

tells.text: The knees bend early instead of staying straight.
Momentum swings the legs up short of 90 degrees, not a controlled lift.

mistake.source: SetForSet Hanging Leg Raise guide: bending the knees before reaching parallel means the straight-leg version is too hard yet; swinging on the bar for momentum cuts the range and turns the set into a momentum move, not a core exercise

sources: Contact fact (hanging swing): a fixed pull-up bar grip (hand_l, hand_r); ExRx notes stall bars keep the upper body still, while a plain bar needs control to minimize the same pendulum swing the mistake shows
